verdict.rationale: Honeycomb documents custom webhooks as a notification target for both Trigger and SLO burn alerts. When alerts fire, it sends JSON payloads to any service that accepts them, and those payloads can be customized with variables, Go template functions and example templates, so a remediation service or agent endpoint can receive them. Missing for 10: no documented example of driving automated remediation or an agent from a webhook, no detail on delivery reliability or authentication (retries, signing), and no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can point alert notifications at webhooks that trigger automated remediation or agents

citations.quote: Set up Triggers and SLOs to alert your team when conditions are met, and route notifications to Slack, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams, or a custom webhook.
Route Honeycomb Trigger and SLO burn alerts to any service that accepts a JSON payload, including third-party tools and custom integrations.
Once configured, Honeycomb sends JSON payloads to your webhook upon alerts firing.
This allows you to build custom integrations that receive JSON payloads from Honeycomb upon alerts firing.
Use variables to customize payloads for your Honeycomb trigger alerts and SLO burn alerts.
Transform JSON template data in your Honeycomb webhook payloads using Go template functions to format, filter, and restructure alert content before delivery.
